items.name: Gemini Decision 1
items.summary: Google's new decision model scores up to 1,000 closed-set questions (yes/no, multiple-choice, rubric scoring) in a single forward pass instead of generating text, returning probabilities in 150-250 ms at $0.10 per million input tokens. Built for the judgement calls inside agents: tool selection, model routing, policy checks and context grading.
items.plain: Google's new Gemini Decision 1 is a faster model for AI agent judgement calls — worth a look if clients are adopting agents.

items.name: Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: Google's strongest model is now generally available to paid developers, enterprises and Google AI Ultra subscribers, pitched as frontier-class for cybersecurity and long-horizon agentic work. The launch also previewed /swarm in Antigravity, letting multiple Carbon agents collaborate on one task.

items.name: Claude Fable 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic's most capable model to date, released alongside the vetted-only Mythos 5.2 twin, with faster outputs and a price cut to $8 per million input tokens. It now tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and leads on agentic coding benchmarks.

items.name: Meta Muse Ember
items.summary: Meta's smallest and most efficient Muse model, built for the repetitive work inside agents: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction and long-document parsing. At $0.10 per million input tokens it matches Claude Haiku 5.5's intelligence score at about a third of the cost per task.

items.name: Ant Ling-3.2-flash
items.summary: Ant Group's inclusionAI launched a 560-billion-parameter multimodal mixture-of-experts model (25B active per token) with a 1-million-token context window, natively handling interleaved text, images and video. Free API access for two weeks, with OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints.
